subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `gateway.peers` and cross-gateway session tools now, and what peer URL, auth, identity, replay, and session-visibility boundary must replace the current single-gateway allowlist?
rationale: This PR adds a new core config/API surface and widens the gateway operator trust boundary; automation can find defects, but cannot choose the product and security model for gateway federation.

options.title: Design core peer contract first
options.body: Define peer identity, URL policy, authorization scopes, replay/idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing core cross-gateway session routing.

options.title: Keep this as an extension bridge
options.body: Leave core session tools gateway-local and add only missing plugin/MCP bridge seams if maintainers want this outside core.

options.title: Defer to the federation FRD
options.body: Pause this implementation until the broader federation tracker settles bridge protocol and identity semantics.

recommendation.title: Design core peer contract first
recommendation.body: Define peer identity, URL policy, authorization scopes, replay/idempotency, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing core cross-gateway session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses gateway URL hardening, operator scope, and session-tool behavior where this history shows the strongest ownership signal.
